abstract: Maintains clinical equipment compliance, oxygen system certification, and intensive care bed capacity
system_message:
You are the Emergency medical transport director (MED). Your responsibilities include overseeing clinical equipment compliance, oxygen system certifications, and intensive care bed capacities aboard candidate emergency evacuation vessels, as well as tracking paramedic staffing drill parameters.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains clinical equipment compliance, oxygen system certification, and intensive care bed capacity（CLIN）
information_points.content:
MED-CLIN-0R6：For the Tiree Sea-Lifeline Monohull, the high-flow piped oxygen system is approved under the medical gas pipeline audit, and the candidate features a dedicated intensive care bed capacity of 4 beds within its treatment salon.
MED-CLIN-G7P：For the Minch Wavemaster Express, the high-flow piped oxygen system is approved based on the Scottish Ambulance Service audit of the onboard medical gas pipeline and vacuum manifold, and the vessel provides a dedicated intensive care bed capacity of 4 beds in its climate-controlled patient treatment salon.
MED-CLIN-WUC：For the Sound of Mull High-Speed Catamaran, the high-flow piped oxygen system is not approved according to the onboard medical gas pipeline audit, and the vessel features a dedicated intensive care bed capacity of 3 beds in its treatment salon.

information_points.title: Paramedic staffing drills（MEDEVAC）
information_points.content:
MED-MEDEVAC-RHP：For the Tiree Sea-Lifeline Monohull, the paramedic shift handover completion time recorded during emergency response changeover drills was 15 min.
MED-MEDEVAC-QGA：Clinical audit logs for the Sound of Mull High-Speed Catamaran document a paramedic shift handover completion time of 25 min during crew changeover drills.
MED-MEDEVAC-BRG：During emergency response crew changeover drills for the Minch Wavemaster Express, the paramedic shift handover completion time was recorded at 20 min.
